title: Larkspur Shipping — integration field capture
content:
Context:
- Initial discovery call with Larkspur Shipping (ops + infra): 2026-03-09. They run a mixed cloud/on-prem fleet for telemetry ingestion and want an LLM assistant for carrier routing recommendations and exception triage. Goal: pilot LLM for operational assistant with private deployment (VPC + customer-managed KMS) and daily throughput ~150k tokens, burst 3x during peak windows.

Stakeholders:
- Rafael Duarte (Head of Platform) — infra owner, cares about KMS, outbound egress policies, and certs.
- Mei Chen (Ops lead) — wants high recall for instructions, low hallucination risk; will own prompt set and acceptance tests.
- Victor Alvarez (Security) — needs FIPS-compliant key handling and audit logs retained 1 year.

Key constraints / requirements captured in call:
- Private deployment behind their VPC, no public egress for payloads. Must support customer-managed HSM/KMS and audit streaming to S3 (GovCloud-style).
- Latency SLO: 95th percentile <= 450ms for short prompts (< 256 tokens) for the assistant endpoint. Average query size expected 80–120 tokens.
- Throughput: steady ~150k tokens/day (~2k reqs/day), with 6–8x spikes during morning rush. Need autoscale/burst capability.
- Data retention: logs for model inputs/outputs stored encrypted in their S3 bucket; Redwood must support customer-side encryption keys.
- Model auditing: Mei insists on a mechanism to freeze exact model version + tokenizer used for a given rollout and to tag eval artifacts with that version.

Technical notes / gotchas flagged during meeting:
- Tokenization mismatch risk: they have pre- and post-processing in Java microservices that currently use Hugging Face tokenizers older version — must validate token counts against Redwood runtime tokenizer for cost SLOing. ACTION: Ethan to run token-diff sample (see Action Items).
- Short-lived instance credentials: their infra uses short-lived IAM tokens via STS; Private deploy must be able to refresh credentials without manual intervention. We should propose a sidecar refresh flow.
- On-prem GPU sizing: they have a single rack with 4x A100s but limited spare capacity. Suggest initial pilot on 1 GPU with model variant quantized to int8. Warn: int8 may show slight regression on instruction-following for rare prompts.
- Embedding strategy: Ops wants semantic search over 2 years of incident logs (~250k docs). We recommended batched embeddings with incremental refresh + prefix caching. Note: storage cost will be significant; propose dense-vector index pruning policy (keep top 3 per hourly digest).
- Fallback policy: They want graceful fallback to a smaller model if load increases or a GPU fails. Need clear behavior: 1) scale to reserved burst pool; 2) fallback to smaller model variant; 3) if neither available, return deterministic canned response with link to ops runbook.

Security/compliance specifics:
- HSM/KMS: Victor requires that envelope encryption occurs client-side (customer-managed keys). Redwood needs to support key wrapping with customer's KMS.
- Audit logs: must be exported to their S3 in an encrypted form with a specific prefix and include request-id, model version, token count, and user-id.
- Data residency: they want EU-only compute for EU customers; pilot limited to US, but plan to require region pinning later.

Acceptance criteria (pilot):
- Latency: 95p <= 450ms for 80% of short prompts across a 72-hour window.
- Quality: on their 120-case prompt set, hallucination rate <= 8% and critical-mistake rate = 0.
- Security: end-to-end encryption with customer KMS + audit exports verified for 7 days.
- Operational: autoscaling responds to 6x load within 90s and fallback behavior triggers correctly in simulated GPU failure.

Suggested pilot architecture (sketch):
- Private control plane in Redwood-managed subnet, model egress blocked; compute in customer VPC via deployed agents.
- Sidecar credential refresher (STS logic) + KMS wrapper that performs envelope encryption before logs leave host.
- Cache layer: local KV cache for recent KV cache snapshots for chat sessions to reduce cold-token costs.
- Monitoring: push traces to their Datadog account; use per-route token metrics + alert when unit-cost exceeds threshold.

Action items & owners (short):
- Ethan Cole: run tokenization parity test between Larkspur tokenizer (they'll provide JAR) and Redwood tokenizer; deliver sample diff by 2026-03-13.
- Maya Desai (me): draft pilot SOW (scope + success criteria + pricing sketch for reserved burst) and share with Rafael by 2026-03-14.
- Priya Nair: prototype fallback policy demo (canary to smaller model) and scripted test to simulate GPU failure; deliver demo by 2026-03-20.
- Jonas Berg: check compatibility with our HSM abstraction and produce short note on required changes for envelope encryption integration; due 2026-03-16.
- Larkspur infra: provide sample logs, tokenizer artifact, and S3 bucket ACLs by 2026-03-15.

Open questions / uncertainties to resolve with Larkspur:
- Do they require FIPS-certified HSM nodes for the entire stack or only for key wrapping? (Victor to confirm.)
- Exact retention window for raw payloads vs derived metrics; compliance may require shorter raw payload retention.
- If we quantize model to int8, do they accept a potential ~2–4% drop on a small subset of prompts? Need explicit sign-off from Mei.

Meeting notes / conversational snippets (useful context):
- Rafael: "We can't have any outgoing traffic that hasn't been explicitly approved — even telemetry needs an allowlist."
- Mei: "If the assistant suggests the wrong carrier, that might cause a real missed SLA — so we need conservative defaults and confidence thresholds."
- Victor: "Auditability is non-negotiable. We need to be able to prove which model version answered a case six months from now."

Next meeting: 2026-03-18, 10:00 PT — technical deep-dive with Rafael + infra + security. Objectives: validate SOW assumptions, walk proto for token parity, confirm KMS integration pattern.

Notes to self:
- Keep SOW modular: base private deployment + optional embedding index as add-on.
- Pricing: propose two options — reserved light (steady) + burst credits or flat monthly for pilot.
- Prepare sample canned-response templates for fallback (ops-approved copy).

Quick links to paste into email:
- Token parity checklist (Ethan): https://gist.github.com/maya/token-parity-checklist
- Pilot SOW template: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SE/Pilot+SOW+templates

Misc scratch lines (junk):
- confirm whether they use segmenting=sentence vs token for chunking
- test with embedded search similarity threshold 0.74 to start
- ask legal if 1-year audit retention triggers different contract clause

End of notes.
